topic_summary: This paper presents an on-the-fly machine learning force field (MLFF) method using Bayesian inference integrated into electronic-structure code (VASP). The method automatically generates ML force fields during molecular dynamics simulations, executing first-principles calculations only for new configurations outside existing datasets. Applied to melting point calculations of Al, Si, Ge, Sn, and MgO, the method bypasses >99% of first-principles calculations, achieving ~1000× acceleration while maintaining quantitative accuracy validated by thermodynamic perturbation theory.
key_points: On-the-fly MLFF generation using Bayesian inference during MD simulations
Automatic data selection: FP calculations executed only for out-of-distribution configurations
~1000× simulation acceleration compared to direct FP calculations
Application to melting points of Al, Si, Ge, Sn, and MgO
Validation via thermodynamic perturbation theory confirming quantitative reproduction of FP melting points
